review_cost.rationale: Approve after a round of nits: nothing structural, all changes localized, and the framework usage is already aligned so refactors would be small.

findings.issue: The response cache Map only overwrites entries on re-request and never sweeps expired ones; memory is bounded by the API's URL cardinality (~2k URLs) today, but any new endpoint or growth makes it a slow leak, and expired-plus-never-revisited entries retain their payloads forever.
findings.suggestion: Add a periodic sweep or simple LRU cap (e.g. evict oldest when size exceeds a few thousand) alongside the existing TTL.

findings.issue: Filter state is managed with uncontrolled inputs, three refs, a shared debounce ref and two mount/update effects that hand-sync DOM values with the URL (including a document.activeElement check), instead of useSearchParams with controlled inputs.
findings.suggestion: Use useSearchParams as the source of truth with controlled inputs and derive the query string from it; keep only the debounce as custom code. The pre-hydration-input edge case can be handled with a small, isolated effect.

findings.issue: The catch-all route's component returns null and its loader throws so the root ErrorBoundary renders the 404 UI, which is exported from root.tsx; a reader can't find the not-found UI where they expect it, and genuine loader errors are visually indistinguishable from 404s in code flow.
findings.suggestion: Render the NotFound UI in the catch-all route's default export (with its own <title>), and keep the root ErrorBoundary for unexpected errors; or at least add a comment in not-found.tsx pointing at root.tsx.

findings.issue: The Move shape is declared twice, here and in routes/move.tsx:12-22, with overlapping fields; they will drift when the API shape changes.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared Move type into lib/types.ts alongside Card/TypeInfo.

findings.issue: The ErrorBoundary logs the error only when import.meta.env.DEV, so production errors vanish with no trace on the server.
findings.suggestion: console.error unconditionally in the boundary (or log in the loader/fetch layer) so server-side incidents are diagnosable in production.

findings.issue: parseTeamCookie is invoked in both the root loader and the team loader, so the cookie-reading convention exists in two places.
findings.suggestion: Have the team loader consume the already-parsed team from root loader data via useRouteLoaderData, or keep one server helper and add a comment linking the two uses.

findings.issue: Row keys append the array index (row.name-level i), which weakens React reconciliation and masks duplicate-row bugs; also the sorted useMemo omits the derived columns dependency.
findings.suggestion: Key by row.name (or name+level when needed) and add columns to the memo dependency list.

findings.issue: versionGroupOrders() triggers ~30 parallel version-group fetches outside the shared index cache on first visit to any Pokémon page.
findings.suggestion: Fold version-group orders into the cached getIndex() so cold-start fan-out happens once with the rest of the index.

summary: A clean, current-idiom React Router v8 framework-mode app: proper route modules, generated types, loader-side search params, data() 404s, and a correct custom express server, with the server data layer properly isolated via the .server.ts convention. The team feature integrates well, using a cookie read in the root loader so the UI is SSR-correct with no flash. It merges after a round of small changes: evict cache entries, replace hand-rolled ref/DOM-sync filter plumbing with useSearchParams, and untangle the not-found route arrangement.
